solutions.17: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ, and cos²θ × sec²θ = cos²θ × 1/cos²θ = 1.
solutions.18: tan θ + cot θ = sin θ/cos θ + cos θ/sin θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ) = sec θ cosec θ.
solutions.19: sin 35° = cos 55° and cos 22° = sin 68° (complementary angles). The value is 1 + 1 = 2.
solutions.20: LHS = sin²A + 2 + cosec²A + cos²A + 2 + sec²A = (sin²A + cos²A) + 4 + (1 + cot²A) + (1 + tan²A) = 7 + tan²A + cot²A.
solutions.21: Multiply the numerator and the denominator inside the root by (1 + sin A): √[(1 + sin A)²/(1 − sin²A)] = (1 + sin A)/cos A = sec A + tan A.
solutions.22: cos A/(1 − sin A/cos A) = cos²A/(cos A − sin A). sin A/(1 − cos A/sin A) = sin²A/(sin A − cos A). Sum = (cos²A − sin²A)/(cos A − sin A) = cos A + sin A.
solutions.23: (a) (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, so sec θ − tan θ = 1/p. (b) sec θ = (p + 1/p)/2 and tan θ = (p − 1/p)/2. sin θ = tan θ/sec θ = (p² − 1)/(p² + 1). (c) sin θ = 3/5.

notes.subtitle: Three Identities & Complementary Angles

concepts.title: Basic identity
concepts.text: For every angle θ, sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

concepts.title: Derived identities
concepts.text: Divide by cos²θ: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ. Divide by sin²θ: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

concepts.title: Complementary angles
concepts.text: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

concepts.title: Proving identities
concepts.text: Start with the more complex side, change to sin and cos when needed, and simplify to the other side.

method: Choose the more complicated side.
Write tan, cot, sec and cosec in terms of sin and cos if this helps.
Use an identity to replace 1 − sin²θ, sec²θ − 1 and so on.
Simplify until you get the other side.

practice.question: Prove that (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = sin θ/(1 + cos θ).
If tan θ = 1, find the value of 2sin θ cos θ.

tips: Write each step on a new line.

notes.subtitle: Elevation, Depression & Two-Triangle Problems

concepts.title: Angle of elevation
concepts.text: The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when you look up.

concepts.title: Angle of depression
concepts.text: The angle between the horizontal and the line of sight when you look down. It equals the angle of elevation from the other end.

concepts.title: One-triangle problems
concepts.text: Use tan for height and horizontal distance, sin or cos when the slant length is given.

concepts.title: Two-triangle problems
concepts.text: Write two equations with a common height or distance, and solve them together.

method: Draw a figure and mark the right angles.
Mark the angles and the known lengths.
Write one trigonometric equation for each triangle.
Solve, then round only at the end.

concepts.title: Histogram
concepts.text: Bars without gaps, class intervals on the x-axis and frequencies on the y-axis.

concepts.title: Mode from a histogram
concepts.text: In the tallest bar, draw crossing lines to the corners of the neighbouring bars. The x-value of the crossing point is the mode.

concepts.title: Ogive
concepts.text: Plot the upper class limits against the cumulative frequencies, and join the points with a smooth curve.

notes.subtitle: Mean, Median & Mode

concepts.title: Mean
concepts.text: The mean is the sum of the observations divided by their number. For a frequency table, mean = Σfx/Σf.

concepts.title: Grouped data
concepts.text: Use the class mark of each class as x.

concepts.title: Median
concepts.text: Arrange the data. For odd n, it is the middle value. For even n, it is the mean of the two middle values.

concepts.title: Mode
concepts.text: The value with the highest frequency. For grouped data, the modal class has the highest frequency.

formulas: Median (even n) = mean of (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th values
method: Arrange or tabulate the data.
Find Σf and Σfx for the mean.
Use cumulative frequency to find the median position.
Pick the highest frequency for the mode.

notes.subtitle: Equally Likely Outcomes, Cards, Dice & Coins

concepts.title: Probability
concepts.text: P(E) = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of outcomes, when all outcomes are equally likely.

concepts.title: Range
concepts.text: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. An impossible event has probability 0 and a sure event has probability 1.

concepts.title: Complement
concepts.text: P(not E) = 1 − P(E).

concepts.title: Standard experiments
concepts.text: A die has 6 outcomes, two dice 36, two coins 4, three coins 8. A deck has 52 cards: 4 suits of 13, 12 face cards.

formulas: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
Two dice: 36 outcomes; three coins: 8 outcomes
method: List or count the sample space.
Count the favourable outcomes without double counting.
Write the fraction and simplify it.
Check that the answer is between 0 and 1.
